Note on comparability: Oracle's fiscal year 2024 covers the twelve months ended May 31, 2024 [DOC-1], while Walmart's fiscal year 2024 covers the twelve months ended January 31, 2024 [DOC-2]. These are different fiscal-year periods (a roughly four-month offset), so the growth rates below are not measuring identical calendar periods, even though both are labeled "FY2024."

Calculations:
- Walmart: FY2024 revenue of $642,637 million vs. FY2023 revenue of $605,881 million [DOC-2] → growth = (642,637 − 605,881) / 605,881 ≈ 6.07%
- Oracle: FY2024 revenue of $52,961 million vs. FY2023 revenue of $49,954 million [DOC-1] → growth = (52,961 − 49,954) / 49,954 ≈ 6.02%

Despite the fiscal-year period mismatch noted above, both companies reported very similar year-over-year revenue growth rates in their respective fiscal 2024 filings—Walmart at approximately 6.07% and Oracle at approximately 6.02%, a difference of only about 0.05 percentage points. Walmart's growth was driven off a much larger revenue base (~$606 billion) compared to Oracle's (~$50 billion).

ANSWER: Walmart's FY2024 revenue grew ~6.07% YoY ($605,881M→$642,637M) and Oracle's FY2024 revenue grew ~6.02% YoY ($49,954M→$52,961M) — nearly identical growth rates, though the two companies' fiscal years end on different dates (Jan 31 vs. May 31), so the periods are not perfectly comparable.
